manufacturer_specs.consumption_reference_conditions: Not specified on reviewed manufacturer page

assumptions: 3700 L/min means free air at reference density 1.2 kg/m3
Maximum power and air consumption occur together
Steady motor state and negligible kinetic/potential energy change
25% shaft-power heat return is a sensitivity, not a measurement
22 C is motor inlet, not necessarily scuba tank-to-regulator outlet

conditional_results.tank_reference: Existing 12 L / 200 bar gauge / 30 C initial tank, 20 bar gauge cutoff; adiabatic and isothermal scenarios. Not qualified full-flow runtime.

limitations: Exhaust capture, thread sizes, lubrication, low-temperature and exhaust-backpressure limits unconfirmed
Continuous shaft load up to about 2.7 kW required to reach the screened power
No new nozzle source boundary or CFD validation; do not reuse 77 g/s study as this motor result
listing_conflict: Amazon bullets say 6.3 N m while title/manufacturer imply 13 N m. Use official model data; confirm exact supplied variant.
decision: Credible higher-mass-flow POC candidate if rated supply and continuous shaft load can support it. AM0701 remains simpler for first instrumented bench demonstration. No guaranteed >6 K at 20–50 cm.
